items.title: Do fee-free guarantees for group company loans attract GST? Delhi High Court answers
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday held that a company’s guarantee for a group firm’s loan attracts Goods and Services Tax (GST) even if the company charges no fee for it [Sterlite Power Vs UOI]. The High Court took a view contrary to a Bombay High Court ruling and in line with a verdict delivered by the Gujarat High Court. The Bombay High Court had held that such guarantees fall outside the GST net. A Division Bench of Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Bharat Parashar said the Bombay High Court’s ruling in DP Jain & Co. Infrastructure relied on a Supreme Court decision under the earlier service tax regime, where the payment formed part of the definition of a service. “ The service lies in the assumption of the risk of the related person’s default, and the resulting extension of the guarantor’s creditworthiness to it ,” the Bench said. Justice Anil Kshetrapal The judgment was passed on a batch of petitions filed by Sterlite Power Transmission, ReNew, Jindal Stainless, Azure Power, Essar Power, GAIL and others. The companies argued that a parent company gives a guarantee to protect its investment in a subsidiary and that such a guarantee given without a fee falls outside the GST net. The Hi

items.title: Repayment of fraudulent loan by accused does not end PMLA case against him: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday held that repayment of a loan obtained fraudulently by an accused charged under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) would not erase the money laundering offence against him. [Paulson AJ v. Assistant Director & anr] Justice G Girish made the observation while dismissing three petitions filed by the accused in a money laundering case arising from the alleged financial irregularities at the Karuvannur Service Co-operative Bank. "The contention of the petitioner that the entire loan amount which the petitioner and his relatives availed from the Karuvannoor Service Co-operative Bank Limited had been remitted back, and there is no subsisting liability in that regard, is not a reason to order discharge of the petitioner from the case registered by the Enforcement Directorate." Justice G Girish The case relates to loans sanctioned in violation of banking rules with the involvement of bank officials. The accused and his relatives obtained five loans from the bank totalling ₹2.5 crore in violation of banking rules and used those funds to purchase land, repay debts, renovate his hotel etc. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) provisionally attached

items.title: Ariyil Shukkoor murder: 13 found guilty; CPI(M) leaders Jayarajan, Rajesh acquitted
items.summary: Eighteen accused, including senior leaders of Communist Party of India (Marxist) P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, were acquitted in the murder case of Ariyil Shukkoor, a member of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF). A special CBI court in Kochi on Thursday, November 19, found 13 persons guilty in the case. The quantum of the sentence will be pronounced at 3 PM. Shukkoor, 18, was murdered on February 20, 2012 by a vigilante mob, following an attack on the vehicle used by Jayarajan and Rajesh to visit Pattuvam in Kannur during a League-CPI(M) conflict. Jayarajan, then Kannur district secretary of CPI(M) and Rajesh, then an MLA, were accused of conspiracy in the murder. According to reports, Shukkoor was subjected to a ‘Kangaroo court’ trial for around two hours by the CPI(M) workers before he was stabbed to death. Special judge CBI-III (Ernakulam) P Sabarinathan found accused Sumesh KV, Anoop, Pavithran P, Manoharan PV, NP Ajith Kumar, P P Suresan, EP Radhakrishnan, Shijin Mohan @ Shijin, KV Sajith, VV Mohanan, Purushothaman MV @ Purushu, P K Ajith Kumar, and P P Suresan as guilty.
